newsitem.title: UK: Ford in threat to close north England plant - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ford in threat to close north England plant - paper.

text.p: Ford Motor Co will this week threaten to close its giant Halewood plant in north-western England unless the workforce agrees to new working practices and the loss of more than 500 jobs, the Observer newspaper said. Senior executives would meet trade unions on Thursday for what was described as a crucial meeting for the 4,500 workers at the plant, which the paper said was less efficient than its sister plant at Dagenham in London.

Last week Ford executives said they were talking to Halewood unions about ways of cutting costs and would try to avoid closing plants as they struggled to staunch continuing losses at their European operations.

The Observer said Ford would only agree to make its new Escort model at Halewood if the unions agreed to take part in drastic cost-cutting measures. They might also be asked to approve a two-year no-strike deal.
Ford, which employs around 30,000 workers in Britain, said in September it wanted to cut 1,000 jobs at its British plants through voluntary redundancies and early retirement.
No immediate comment from Ford was available.
